model.name: Classification Binding
model.purpose: Govern the first-class assignment of classification items (codes, concepts, classes) from identified schemes to classifiable subjects, together with the terminology-binding constraints that determine which items may be used, so an agent can create, inspect, validate, version and operate classification assertions independently of storage format.
model.scope_statement: This pattern covers the binding assertion that links a classifiable subject to one or more items in a classification scheme or value set, and the element-level binding policy that constrains allowed items. It records identity of the binding, scheme and item references, lexical forms, role and multiplicity, binding strength, temporal validity, scheme version pinning, provenance of the assignment, authority, validation against the scheme, and interoperability of coded versus textual forms. It does not define the internal structure of a scheme, thesaurus, ontology or statistical classification, which remain composable sibling models.
in_scope: Identity of a classification-binding assertion as a governed record, distinct from the identity of the subject and of the classification item.
Reference to a classification scheme, code system, concept scheme or thesaurus, including its canonical URI and, where required, version.
Reference to a classification scheme item by code, notation, concept IRI or equivalent master identifier.
Human-readable display defined by the scheme and user- or agent-entered text that may stand for or accompany a code.
Element- or attribute-level terminology binding: the value set applied to a slot and the conformance strength of that binding.
Role, facet and multiplicity of an assignment, including primary versus additional class, theme versus type/genre, and keyword type.
Lifecycle of an assignment (active, superseded, withdrawn, dual-running during scheme transition) and effective time of the classification.
Provenance of who or what assigned the class, whether the coding was user-selected, method, evidence and confidence.
Validation that a code belongs to the referenced system or value-set expansion, uniqueness of system-plus-code, and optional mutual-exclusivity rules.
Translations, equivalent codings, and uncoded textual concepts; mappings are referenced, not owned.
Access, privacy, retention and exception handling for sensitive classification assertions.
out_of_scope: Definition, hierarchy, editorial notes and maintenance of a classification scheme, code system, concept scheme, thesaurus or ontology (sibling Concept System / Classification Scheme model).
Definition of a value set as a selectable expansion independent of its application to an element (sibling Value Set model), except the reference from a binding.
Ontological class membership as OWL or RDF Schema typing of the subject (rdf:type / owl:Class), except as an alignment when a SKOS concept is also an OWL class.
Security, confidentiality or dissemination-control labels (TLP, CUI, ISO/IEC 27001 information classification), which are a different sense of classification.
Inter-scheme correspondence tables and SKOS mapping properties as first-class mapping objects (sibling Mapping / Correspondence model), except as referenced evidence that two bindings are comparable.
Physical filing, shelf-mark or records-centre location of an artefact.
Identifier systems (business identifiers, medical record numbers) even when they use a system URI and a value; identifiers are not classification items.
Training, weights or evaluation of a machine-learning classifier, except as provenance of an automated assignment.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Classification Scheme / Concept System / Code System / Statistical Classification
boundary_notes.distinction: ISO/IEC 11179 defines a classification scheme as a concept system used to divide objects into groups, and a classification scheme item as content of that scheme. SKOS defines skos:ConceptScheme and skos:Concept. FHIR separates CodeSystem (defines codes) from ValueSet (selects codes). GSIM defines Statistical Classification and Classification Item. This pattern references those objects; it does not register their internal hierarchy, levels or editorial content.

FHIR binds a value set to an element and states conformance strength. ISO/IEC 11179 distinguishes conceptual domains and value domains from the act of classifying a classifiable item. This pattern records the applied binding (which value set, which strength) and instance membership tests; it does not own value-set compose/expand definitions.

FHIR Identifier uses system plus value to identify an entity; Coding uses system plus code to identify a concept. A classification binding must not be modelled as an identifier, and a date is not an identifier of either.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Resource type / genre (dcterms:type, DCMI Type Vocabulary) versus subject/theme
boundary_notes.distinction: Dublin Core and DCAT 3 treat dcterms:type as nature or genre of the resource and dcat:theme / dcterms:subject as topical classification from a KOS. Both may be realised as classification bindings but they are different facets and must not be collapsed.

ISO 19115 MD_Keywords allows free-text keywords with optional thesaurusName and keywordClass ontology binding. DCAT distinguishes dcat:keyword (literal) from dcat:theme (KOS concept). An uncoded text binding is in scope as a degraded or complementary form; uncontrolled folksonomy governance is not a substitute for a scheme-backed binding.

boundary_notes.neighbor: SKOS / XKOS mapping and GSIM correspondence table
boundary_notes.distinction: skos:exactMatch, broadMatch and related mapping properties, and GSIM correspondence tables, relate items across schemes. They explain how two bindings can be compared; they are not themselves assignments of a class to a subject.

Information-security labels classify sensitivity of a record, not the subject-matter class of the entity. They are excluded. Access control on a subject-matter binding (for example a health diagnosis code) remains in scope as an access concern of this pattern.

SKOS notes that concepts may relate to OWL classes but SKOS is a KOS model, not a formal ontology language. rdf:type membership is ontological typing; a classification binding is an assignment into a scheme used for grouping, discovery or statistical coding and may coexist with typing without being identical to it.

sources.title: Generic Statistical Information Model (version 2.0): User Guide

sources.relevance: International statistical reference model for Statistical Classification, Classification Item, levels, series, versions and correspondence, including assignment of mutually exclusive categories to variables.

bundles.name: Binding identity and classifiable subject
bundles.description: Identity of the classification-binding assertion and of the subject being classified, kept distinct from identifiers of schemes and of classification items.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 11179 registration assigns unique identifiers to registered objects and treats classification as an association to a classifiable item. FHIR and SKOS identify concepts by system-plus-code or URI; the binding itself still needs its own master identifier so assignments can be audited, superseded and retained independently of the subject record projection.

layers.name: Binding assertion identity
layers.description: How a classification binding is identified, named and distinguished from the subject and from the class.

findings.name: Binding record identity
findings.description: A classification binding is a first-class assertion with its own identifier. Identity priority is the authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the registry or terminology service; then a governed global IRI; then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. A date, display string or code is not an identifier of the binding.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this classification-binding assertion, and which registry or terminology service issued it?
What governed global IRI, if any, identifies this binding assertion independently of storage format?
If no master-system identifier or IRI exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and when was it assigned?
Has the implementation incorrectly used the classification code, a date, or a display label as the binding identifier?

data_elements.name: Binding master identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the binding assertion in the master registry or terminology service.

data_elements.name: Binding IRI
data_elements.description: Optional governed global IRI for the binding assertion.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Fallback unique identifier assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master identifier exists.

artifacts.name: Classification binding identity record
artifacts.description: Governed identity stub for the binding assertion, including master id, IRI and Dimension UUID.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Prefer issuing-registry master identifier; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID or ULID. Never a date or code.

layers.name: Classifiable subject
layers.description: The object, dataset, person, variable, metadata item or other entity to which the class is assigned.

findings.name: Subject of classification
findings.description: ISO/IEC 11179 allows any metadata item to be a classifiable item. DCAT classifies catalogued resources; FHIR codes elements of resources; GSIM assigns classification items to variables and units of observation. The subject reference must identify the classified entity without embedding the scheme.

questions.text: Which subject is classified, and what is its master identifier or IRI?
What kind of classifiable item is it (resource, dataset, person, organisation, variable, metadata item, geospatial record, or other)?
If the binding constrains or fills a specific element, attribute or variable, which slot on the subject is bound?
Does the binding apply to the whole subject or only to a part, version, observation or geographic coverage of it?

data_elements.name: Subject reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the classifiable entity.

data_elements.name: Subject kind
data_elements.description: Kind of classifiable item.

data_elements.name: Bound slot or variable
data_elements.description: Element path, attribute or statistical variable to which the binding applies, when not the whole subject.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The subject is referenced, not copied; its canonical description lives in the subject’s own model. The binding stores only identifiers, kind and optional slot path.

bundles.name: Scheme, item and lexical form
bundles.description: The classification scheme, the item assigned from it, and the lexical codes and labels carried on the binding.
bundles.rationale: FHIR requires a code-system URI plus a code for unambiguous concept identity. SKOS identifies concepts by URI, places them in schemes, and allows notations and multilingual labels. ISO/IEC 11179 names classification scheme items as nodes or terms in a scheme. DCAT recommends SKOS concepts linked to a catalog theme taxonomy.

layers.name: Scheme and classification item
layers.description: Canonical identification of the scheme and of the item used in the binding.

findings.name: Classification scheme reference
findings.description: The scheme is a code system, concept scheme, thesaurus, taxonomy, ontology or statistical classification identified by a stable URI or registry identifier. FHIR requires the system URI to identify a code system, not a value set. DCAT attaches a theme taxonomy to a catalog as a KOS. ISO 19115 cites a thesaurus by CI_Citation on MD_Keywords.

questions.text: What canonical URI or master identifier identifies the classification scheme or code system, and has an authoritative naming system confirmed it?
What kind of scheme is referenced (controlled vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, ontology, statistical classification, or uncontrolled list)?
Does the stored system identifier point at a code system or concept scheme rather than at a value set or expansion URL?
Which organisation maintains the scheme and is it an official, community or local scheme for this binding’s jurisdiction?

data_elements.name: Scheme URI
data_elements.description: Canonical URI of the code system, concept scheme or equivalent KOS.

data_elements.name: Scheme kind
data_elements.description: Type of classification scheme.

data_elements.name: Scheme citation
data_elements.description: Bibliographic or registry citation of the scheme or thesaurus, including title.

artifacts.name: Scheme citation
artifacts.description: Citation or naming-system record used to pin the scheme identity and maintainer.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Canonical scheme URI or code-system URL as master; citation title is a designation, not an identifier.

findings.name: Classification item, code and concept
findings.description: The assigned item is identified as the unique pair of system URI and code in FHIR, as a SKOS concept IRI (optionally with notation), or as an ISO/IEC 11179 classification scheme item. A code may be a predefined token or a post-coordinated expression in the system’s syntax. Concept permanence cannot be assumed across versions.

questions.text: What code, notation or concept IRI identifies the classification item within the scheme?
Is the combination of scheme identifier and item code unique, and is a scheme version required because the system does not guarantee concept permanence?
Is the code a precoordinated concept or a post-coordinated expression in the scheme’s syntax, and is that expression valid?
Is the concept asserted to be in the referenced scheme (skos:inScheme or equivalent), and does that assertion match the scheme URI on the binding?

data_elements.name: Item code
data_elements.description: Symbol in the syntax defined by the scheme.

data_elements.name: Concept IRI
data_elements.description: URI identifying the SKOS or equivalent concept, when the scheme publishes IRIs.

data_elements.name: Notation
data_elements.description: Lexical classification code distinct from preferred labels, as in SKOS notation.

data_elements.name: Coordination mode
data_elements.description: Whether the code is precoordinated or a compositional expression.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The classification item is referenced from the scheme; the binding stores identifiers, codes and notations rather than copying the item’s definitional artefact.

layers.name: Display, text and language
layers.description: Scheme-defined displays, user text, and language-tagged labels.

findings.name: Display, user text and language
findings.description: FHIR Coding.display is the representation defined by the system; CodeableConcept.text is the human language representation selected or uttered by the user. Computation on display alone is unsafe. SKOS separates prefLabel, altLabel and hiddenLabel with language tags. DCMI prefers a URI for subject but allows a literal if needed.

questions.text: What display string does the referenced scheme define for this item, in which language, and is it the scheme’s recommended display?
What text did the user or agent enter as the intended meaning, and does it stand alone without a code?
Are preferred labels unique per language within the scheme, and has any process treated display text as a computable identifier?
If no code is present, is a literal subject or keyword recorded, and is it preferred to be aligned later to a controlled vocabulary URI?

data_elements.name: Scheme display
data_elements.description: Human-readable representation defined by the scheme.

data_elements.name: User or agent concept text
data_elements.description: Text as seen, selected or uttered, representing intended meaning.

data_elements.name: Preferred label
data_elements.description: SKOS preferred lexical label with language tag.

data_elements.name: Language tag
data_elements.description: BCP 47 language tag for display or text.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Labels and user text are inline lexical data on the binding; scheme-wide label integrity is enforced by the scheme sibling model.

bundles.name: Binding constraint, role and facet
bundles.description: The policy that constrains allowed items for a slot, and the role or facet of an instance assignment.
bundles.rationale: FHIR defines binding as applying a value set to an element with a strength. DCAT allows multiple themes and separately types genre. ISO 19115 types keywords (theme, place, discipline, taxon and others) and provides a high-level topic category list that is known to overlap. GSIM statistical classifications are typically mutually exclusive and exhaustive for a variable.

layers.name: Element terminology binding
layers.description: Constraints that apply a value set to a slot and state how strictly instances must follow it.

findings.name: Value set applied to a slot
findings.description: A terminology binding names the value set whose expansion is the allowed or suggested set of codes for an element. The value-set canonical URL is not the code-system URL. Additional bindings may tighten the main binding in a context.

questions.text: Which value-set canonical URL is bound to this element or slot, and is it version-pinned?
Is the bound object a value set rather than a code system, and which code systems does that value set draw from?
Are additional bindings defined for particular usage contexts, and what is each additional binding’s purpose?
What human-readable description states the intent of this element binding for implementers?

data_elements.name: Value set canonical URL
data_elements.description: Canonical identifier of the bound value set, optionally with version.

data_elements.name: Bound element path
data_elements.description: Path of the element or attribute to which the value set is bound.

data_elements.name: Additional bindings
data_elements.description: Context-specific extra bindings with purpose codes.

artifacts.name: Element binding specification
artifacts.description: The binding fragment of an element definition, profile or application profile that applies a value set and strength to a slot.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Canonical URL of the StructureDefinition or profile plus element path; version of the profiling artefact.

findings.name: Binding strength and conformance
findings.description: FHIR binding strength states conformance: required (instance SHALL be from the value set), extensible (SHALL be from the value set if any code applies, else alternate coding or text), preferred (encouraged but not required), or example (illustrative only). Strength is a property of the element binding, not of a single assigned code.

questions.text: What binding strength applies to this slot, using the required, extensible, preferred or example codes?
If strength is required, does every populated instance contain a code from the bound expansion?
If strength is extensible and no bound code applies, what alternate coding or text was used and who reviewed that the value set did not cover the concept?
If strength is example, are instances still expected to record a scheme and code when known, rather than treating the example set as closed?

data_elements.name: Binding strength
data_elements.description: required | extensible | preferred | example.

data_elements.name: Conformance result
data_elements.description: Outcome of testing an instance against the bound expansion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Binding strength is a closed code from http://hl7.org/fhir/binding-strength stored on the element-binding specification; no separate artefact is required beyond that specification.

layers.name: Role, facet and multiplicity
layers.description: Why this class is attached and whether multiple classes may coexist.

findings.name: Classification role, facet and multiplicity
findings.description: A binding has a role or facet: topical theme, type/genre, ISO 19115 keyword type, statistical variable coding, or local primary/secondary rank. DCAT allows multiple themes. GSIM statistical classifications used as variable domains are typically mutually exclusive and exhaustive. ISO 19115 topic categories explicitly overlap and the user is asked to pick the most appropriate. These rules conflict and must be recorded as policy on the slot, not assumed globally.

questions.text: What facet or role does this binding play (subject/theme, type/genre, place, discipline, taxon, statistical variable, or other keyword type)?
Is this the primary classification for the facet, a secondary class, or an unordered additional theme?
Does the slot allow multiple simultaneous classes, require mutual exclusivity, or require a single most-appropriate class despite known overlap?
If both a type/genre and a subject/theme are recorded, are they separate bindings rather than one overloaded code?

data_elements.name: Classification facet
data_elements.description: Role of the binding (theme, type, place, statistical domain, and so on).

data_elements.name: Primary classification flag
data_elements.description: Whether this assignment is the primary class for the facet.

data_elements.name: Multiplicity policy
data_elements.description: Whether the slot is single-valued, multi-valued, mutually exclusive, or overlap-tolerant.

data_elements.name: Keyword type
data_elements.description: ISO 19115 MD_KeywordTypeCode when the binding is a geospatial keyword.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role, rank and multiplicity are attributes of the binding and of the slot policy, stored inline.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, time and scheme version
bundles.description: State of the assignment over time, effective periods, dual-running during scheme transitions, and pinning of scheme versions.
bundles.rationale: FHIR recommends exchanging code-system version when meaning is not guaranteed across releases. GSIM treats versions of a Statistical Classification as first-class objects and documents item change types. SKOS history notes document concept change. Registry identification is not a date. Event time and ingestion time must be recorded separately in RFC 3339 form.

layers.name: Assignment lifecycle and effective time
layers.description: Status and temporal applicability of a particular binding assertion.

findings.name: Assignment status and effective period
findings.description: A binding may be proposed, active, superseded, withdrawn, or retained for history after the subject is reclassified. Effective time is the period during which the class applied to the subject (event time). Observation or ingestion time is when the assertion was recorded. Dual bindings to successive scheme versions are a recognised transition case in statistical classifications.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle status of this binding assertion (proposed, active, superseded, withdrawn, historical)?
Over what inclusive start and optional end instants did this class apply to the subject, recorded as RFC 3339 date-times with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
When was the binding observed or ingested, as distinct from the event time at which the class applied?
During a scheme revision, is a dual binding to the predecessor and successor classifications required, and which correspondence supports that pair?
If the assigned code has since been retired or combined in a later scheme version, is the historical binding preserved rather than rewritten?

data_elements.name: Assignment status
data_elements.description: Lifecycle status of the binding assertion.

data_elements.name: Effective start
data_elements.description: Instant the classification began to apply to the subject.

data_elements.name: Effective end
data_elements.description: Instant the classification ceased to apply; absent means still applicable or end unknown.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: When the assertion was recorded, distinct from effective time.

data_elements.name: Superseding binding
data_elements.description: Reference to the binding that replaces this one.

artifacts.name: Reclassification event record
artifacts.description: Event that ends one binding and optionally starts another, including dual-running pairs during scheme revision.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Event identifier from the master audit or registry; timestamps are RFC 3339 values, not identifiers.

layers.name: Scheme version and concept permanence
layers.description: Whether the binding pins a scheme version and why.

findings.name: Scheme version pinning and concept permanence
findings.description: FHIR says a well-maintained code system may not need version on each Coding, but version SHOULD be exchanged when meaning is not consistent across releases, and SHALL be used when CodeSystem.versionNeeded is true. GSIM treats each Statistical Classification version as its own object. Virtual changes alter codes or names without changing meaning; real changes, deletions, creations and combinations do. Bindings must record which version was used when choosing the code.

questions.text: Which version of the scheme was used when this code was chosen, and is version mandatory because the system requires it?
Does this scheme guarantee concept permanence across versions, and if not, what happens to historical bindings when items change?
If the item changed between versions, was the change virtual (code or name only) or a real semantic change, combination or split?
Should this binding be retargeted to a successor item, left on the original version, or dual-coded?

data_elements.name: Scheme version
data_elements.description: Version string of the code system or statistical classification used when choosing the code.

data_elements.name: Version needed flag
data_elements.description: Whether the scheme requires version on instance codings.

data_elements.name: Item change type
data_elements.description: GSIM-aligned change category when comparing versions.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Version strings and change types are inline attributes of the binding; the scheme version artefact itself belongs to the Classification Scheme sibling model.

bundles.name: Provenance, authority and quality
bundles.description: Who assigned the class, by what method, with what evidence and confidence, under whose authority, and who owns the binding.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 11179 states that registration provides identification, provenance and quality monitoring. FHIR records whether a coding was user-selected. ISO 19115 keywordClass can bind keywords to an ontology for semantic processing. Official statistical and geospatial classifications have designated maintainers and jurisdictions.

findings.name: Classifier, method, evidence and confidence
findings.description: A binding records the agent that assigned the class, whether the coding was chosen directly by a user, whether a human reviewed an extensible-binding exception, the method (manual pick-list, rule, statistical coding index, or algorithm), supporting evidence, and any confidence measure. Primary standards define userSelected and provenance of metadata; they do not standardise ML confidence calibration, which remains an evidence gap.

questions.text: Which person, organisation or software agent assigned this classification, and under what role?
Was this coding chosen directly by a user from a pick list, or inferred, mapped or algorithmically assigned?
What evidence supports the assignment (observed characteristic, coding index entry, document excerpt, rule identifier)?
What confidence or quality measure accompanies an automated assignment, and is that measure standardised or locally defined?
If the assignment is automated or uses an extensible extra code, who reviewed it and with what outcome?

data_elements.name: Classifier agent
data_elements.description: Person, organisation or system that made the assignment.

data_elements.name: User selected
data_elements.description: True if the coding was chosen directly by a user.

data_elements.name: Assignment method
data_elements.description: Manual, index lookup, rule, or algorithmic method.

data_elements.name: Confidence measure
data_elements.description: Local or standard confidence of an automated assignment.

data_elements.name: Evidence references
data_elements.description: Supporting observations, excerpts or rules.

artifacts.name: Assignment provenance record
artifacts.description: Provenance of the classification act, including agent, method, evidence and review.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Provenance record identifier from the master provenance store; not the subject id and not the code.

layers.name: Authority, ownership and jurisdiction
layers.description: Who may authorise a scheme and who owns the binding record.

findings.name: Authority, ownership and jurisdiction
findings.description: FHIR routes external code-system URIs through HL7 Terminology Authority where listed. Statistical classifications such as ISIC have UN custodianship; regional schemes (NACE, NAICS) apply in particular jurisdictions. ISO/IEC 11179 registration records stewardship of classified items. Ownership of the binding record is the adopting Dimension’s data owner, which is not necessarily the scheme maintainer.

questions.text: Who is the custodial authority of the referenced scheme, and is the URI the one authorised by that authority or by a naming system such as HL7 THO/HTA?
Which party owns this binding record in the adopting Dimension, and who may update or withdraw it?
In which jurisdiction or statistical territory is this classification valid (for example NAICS versus NACE versus ISIC)?
Is this assignment an official legal or statistical coding, a community convention, or a local convenience class?

data_elements.name: Scheme custodian
data_elements.description: Organisation that maintains the scheme.

data_elements.name: Binding owner
data_elements.description: Party that owns the binding record in the Dimension.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Territory or statistical area in which the scheme applies.

data_elements.name: Official status
data_elements.description: Whether the assignment is official, community or local.

artifacts.name: Scheme authorisation or official coding notice
artifacts.description: Evidence that a scheme URI is authorised or that an assignment is an official coding for a jurisdiction.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Custodian register identifier or legal instrument identifier; dates of effect are timestamps, not identifiers.

bundles.name: Validation, interoperability and governance
bundles.description: Integrity of coded values, translations and mappings, uncoded text, access, privacy, retention and bootstrap contracts.
bundles.rationale: FHIR treats system-plus-code as the unique concept identity and warns that display-only computation is unsafe. CodeableConcept allows multiple Codings as translations plus text. SKOS mapping properties relate concepts across schemes. DCAT and DCMI prefer KOS URIs but allow keywords or literals. Access and retention follow registry quality and privacy of sensitive codes.

layers.name: Integrity and membership validation
layers.description: Checks that an instance coding is well formed and in the intended set.

findings.name: Membership, integrity and exclusivity checks
findings.description: Validate that a coding has a known system URI, that the code exists in that system version, that it is in the bound value-set expansion when strength requires it, that display is not used as a key, and that mutual-exclusivity policy for the slot is satisfied. Case sensitivity of system URIs is required; case sensitivity of codes is defined by the code system.

questions.text: Does the code exist in the stated system and version, and was the expansion or code-system snapshot used for the check recorded?
If a required or extensible binding applies, is the code in the value-set expansion, and what expansion identifier and timestamp were used?
Has any consumer used display or text as a join key instead of system plus code or concept IRI?
If the slot requires mutually exclusive categories, do multiple active bindings for the same facet violate that rule?
Are system URIs compared case-sensitively, and does the code system declare whether its codes are case-sensitive?

data_elements.name: Membership result
data_elements.description: Outcome of testing code-in-system and code-in-value-set.

data_elements.name: Value-set expansion identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the expansion used for a membership test.

data_elements.name: Integrity flags
data_elements.description: Flags for display-as-key, missing system, empty code, exclusivity violation.

artifacts.name: Classification binding validation report
artifacts.description: Record of membership, expansion and exclusivity checks against a stated scheme version and value-set expansion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Report identifier plus binding master id; include expansion timestamp as RFC 3339 observation time.

layers.name: Translations, access and retention
layers.description: Cross-scheme encodings, uncoded text, access control and retention of bindings.

findings.name: Translations, mappings and uncoded text
findings.description: A CodeableConcept may carry several Codings as translations of one concept plus text. SKOS mapping properties and GSIM correspondence tables relate items across schemes and are referenced, not duplicated. Uncoded text or dcat:keyword remains a valid degraded form when a URI is not feasible, with recommended later alignment.

questions.text: Which additional codings are translations of the same concept, and which coding is user-selected or preferred for exchange?
What mapping or correspondence, if any, justifies treating two items from different schemes as comparable on this subject?
If only a free-text keyword or literal subject is present, what controlled-vocabulary alignment is planned and who owns that gap?
When projecting to DCAT, is dcat:theme used for KOS concepts and dcat:keyword for literals, without assuming a fixed OWL range for theme?

data_elements.name: Additional codings
data_elements.description: Translation or equivalent Coding entries for the same concept.

data_elements.name: Mapping or correspondence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a SKOS mapping or GSIM correspondence used as justification.

data_elements.name: Uncoded keyword or literal subject
data_elements.description: Literal used when a concept URI is not available.

artifacts.name: Coding translation set
artifacts.description: Bundle of equivalent or translated Codings for one concept on one subject, with optional mapping references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The parent binding master identifier; member codings are identified by system plus code, not by display.

findings.name: Access, privacy, retention and exceptions
findings.description: Some classification bindings (for example health, intelligence, or personal characteristics) are sensitive even though they are not security labels. Access is by default deny-outside-role. Retention of historical bindings is required for audit and statistical revision; deletion is an explicit, justified exception.

questions.text: Is this binding sensitive personal, health, or otherwise restricted classification, and which access scope applies?
Which roles may read, create, update or withdraw this binding, and what is logged?
How long must historical bindings be retained after supersession, and under what legal or statistical hold?
When is deletion of a binding permitted (for example erasure right) and what tombstone or justification remains?

data_elements.name: Sensitivity flag
data_elements.description: Whether the binding is restricted personal or otherwise sensitive.

data_elements.name: Access scope
data_elements.description: bundle, layer, finding or artefact scope of access control.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration or policy identifier for keeping superseded bindings.

data_elements.name: Deletion basis
data_elements.description: Legal or policy basis for erasure, if any.

artifacts.name: Binding access and retention policy
artifacts.description: Policy stating who may access classification bindings, how long superseded assignments are kept, and deletion exceptions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Policy identifier in the Dimension policy register.

functions.name: Assign classification
functions.description: Create a binding assertion that classifies a subject with a scheme item or uncoded text, recording identity, scheme, item, facet, provenance and observation time.
preconditions: If coded, scheme URI identifies a code system or concept scheme, not a value set.
Slot multiplicity and exclusivity policy permit an additional active binding.
effects: A new binding assertion is registered with master identity.
Audit provenance of the assignment is recorded.
If exclusivity applies, conflicting active bindings for the same facet are superseded.

functions.name: Apply element terminology binding
functions.description: Attach a value set and binding strength to a slot so later instance assignments can be validated.
preconditions: Value set canonical URL is not used as a code-system URI.
Strength is one of required, extensible, preferred, example.
effects: Subsequent instance assignments to the slot are judged against this binding.
Conformance rules for required and extensible strengths become enforceable.

functions.name: Validate coding against scheme and binding
functions.description: Test that a coding’s system-plus-code exists in the stated version and, if applicable, in the bound value-set expansion, without using display as a key.
preconditions: System URI is present for coded bindings.
Expansion or code-system snapshot is identified when strength requires membership.
effects: Conformance result is recorded with expansion observation time.

functions.name: Record translation or mapped coding
functions.description: Add an additional Coding as a translation of the same concept, or attach a reference to a correspondence that justifies a cross-scheme code.
preconditions: Additional coding identifies a concept in its own scheme.
Mapping type is recorded when schemes differ.
effects: CodeableConcept-style multiple encodings are available for interoperability.
Preferred or user-selected coding is explicit.

functions.name: Supersede, withdraw or dual-run a binding
functions.description: End an assignment, replace it after reclassification or scheme revision, or keep dual bindings during a transition.
preconditions: Caller is authorised to update the binding.
Timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z.
effects: Dual-running predecessor and successor may both be active for a defined period.

functions.name: Pin or retarget scheme version
functions.description: Record the scheme version used when choosing a code, or decide whether to retarget a binding after a real or virtual item change.
preconditions: Scheme versionNeeded or lack of concept permanence has been assessed.
effects: Historical meaning of the code remains reconstructable.
Virtual changes can keep meaning while updating notation.

functions.name: Query subjects by classification
functions.description: Find classifiable subjects that have active bindings to a given item, including optional broader-closure if the scheme supplies hierarchy and policy allows inference.
preconditions: Query uses system plus code or concept IRI, not display text.
Broader closure is used only when the scheme’s hierarchical relations are in scope and authorised.
effects: Returns current assignments without rewriting historical bindings.

functions.name: Align uncoded text to a scheme item
functions.description: Propose or apply a controlled concept URI or code for a literal subject or keyword.
preconditions: Target scheme is authorised for the facet.
effects: Degraded keyword form is upgraded or a tracked gap remains with an owner.

composition.target: Classification Scheme / Concept System / Code System / Statistical Classification
composition.purpose: Identify the KOS from which the assigned item is drawn; the scheme’s internal hierarchy, levels and editorial content remain in the sibling model.

composition.target: Classification Item / SKOS Concept / CodeSystem concept
composition.purpose: Identify the assigned class by concept IRI, code or notation.
Name the set of codes an element binding applies to a slot, distinct from the code system that defines those codes.

composition.target: Classifiable subject (dataset, resource, party, variable, metadata item, geospatial record)
composition.purpose: Identify the object being classified without absorbing that object’s native model.
Record classifier, owner, scheme custodian and reviewer.
Attach assignment method, evidence, observation time and review without replacing the binding’s own identity.
Justify cross-scheme translations and dual-running during revisions without treating mappings as subject classifications.
Align concept IRI, inScheme, notation and labels; do not treat SKOS mapping properties as assignment bindings.
Align instance shape (system, version, code, display, userSelected, text) and element binding strength. Alignment is not a claim of FHIR conformance for a Dimension implementation.

composition.target: ISO/IEC 11179 classification scheme and classification scheme item
composition.purpose: Align the association from a classifiable item to a scheme item; the 11179 registry metamodel remains the authority for registry-item classification.

composition.target: DCAT dcat:theme, dcat:themeTaxonomy, dcat:keyword and dcterms:type
composition.purpose: Align thematic KOS classification, catalog taxonomies, free-text keywords and type/genre as distinct facets.
Align geospatial keyword bindings, thesaurus citations, ontology-backed keyword classes and high-level topic categories.

composition.target: GSIM Statistical Classification and Classification Item
composition.purpose: Align statistical coding of variables, mutual exclusivity, versions and item-change typology.
Keep business identifiers (system plus value) distinct from classification items (system plus code).

owner_package_requirements: Designate a party as owner and steward of Classification Binding records in the adopting Dimension.
Publish a namespace IRI under which binding assertions, element-binding specifications and validation reports are identified.
Declare the authorised classification schemes, naming systems and value sets that may appear on bindings, including jurisdictional scope.
State multiplicity and mutual-exclusivity policy per facet and slot.
Require AGENTS.md bootstrap fields before any MongoDB, MCP or file projection is used.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint binding IRIs as {dimension-namespace}/xct/cls/binding/{master-id} and element-binding IRIs as {dimension-namespace}/xct/cls/element-binding/{profile}/{element-path}. Do not use classification codes, dates or display strings as path segments that serve as identifiers. Scheme and concept IRIs remain those assigned by scheme custodians or authorised naming systems.
registry_links: Alignments: SKOS ConceptScheme, FHIR Coding/CodeableConcept/binding-strength, ISO/IEC 11179 classification scheme item, DCAT theme, ISO 19115 MD_Keywords, GSIM Statistical Classification

canonicalization_rules: Canonical coded identity is scheme URI plus code, or concept IRI when the scheme publishes IRIs; trim and case-fold only as the scheme specifies. System URIs are always case-sensitive.
Do not canonicalise on display, preferred label or user text.
Element bindings canonicalise to value-set canonical URL plus element path plus strength, not to a code-system URL.
Facet (theme versus type versus statistical domain) is part of canonical comparison so two facets on one subject are not merged.
Timestamps canonicalise to RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z.
patch_rules: Patches may add translations, pin a scheme version, or update display copies; they must not silently change system plus code.
Status transitions to superseded or withdrawn require a reclassification event and must not delete the original identifier.
Extensible extra codes require a recorded human-review exception.
Uncoded text may be patched to a coded item only with an alignment event and reviewer.
compatibility_rules: A required binding remaining required with a narrower value set is a breaking change for instances.
Widening from required to extensible or preferred is compatible for existing instance codes that remain in the old set.
Scheme version retargeting after a real semantic change is a breaking reinterpretation and must dual-run or explicitly supersede.
DCAT projections must not assume a fixed range of skos:Concept on dcat:theme.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier of the binding or of the element-binding specification.
Governed global IRI in the Dimension namespace or custodian namespace.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. A date, code, notation or display string is not an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record assignment event time and observation or ingestion time separately as RFC 3339 date-times with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts (validation reports, reclassification events, policy versions) use {artifact-kind}-{master-id}-v{n} or an equivalent sequential register number; n is not a date.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Integrity is the tuple of binding id plus scheme URI plus code (or concept IRI) plus facet; checksums cover that tuple and provenance, not display text.

policies: Default: a coded binding SHALL include a code-system or concept-scheme URI; value-set URLs SHALL NOT be stored as system.
Default: membership in a required binding is tested against a recorded value-set expansion; display-only matching is prohibited.
Historical bindings are retained after supersession for the Dimension retention period unless a recorded erasure exception applies.
Sensitive classification bindings (health, personal characteristics, restricted topics) are confidential by default and are not security-label substitutes.

read: Any agent with finding-scope read may resolve non-sensitive bindings by master id, subject, or system-plus-code.
Sensitive bindings require role-justified access and are fully audited.
create: Steward or assigning agent may create a binding if the scheme is authorised and slot policy allows.
Element-binding specifications are created only by the profile or scheme steward.
update: Display, translations, version pin and provenance may be updated in place.
Changes to system plus code require supersession, not in-place rewrite, except to correct a documented transcription error with audit.
delete: Hard delete is exceptional and requires a recorded legal or policy basis plus a tombstone.
Supersession and withdrawal are the normal end-of-life operations.

roles.name: Classification steward
responsibilities: Own binding records in the Dimension.

roles.name: Scheme authority
responsibilities: Maintain the referenced classification scheme or statistical classification.
Publish canonical URIs, versions and concept permanence rules.

roles.name: Terminology service operator
responsibilities: Preserve expansion snapshots used for conformance tests.

roles.name: Auditor
responsibilities: Review automated assignments and sensitive bindings.
Verify that display is not used as a key and that retention holds are honoured.

roles.name: Subject data owner
responsibilities: Invoke erasure exceptions where law requires deletion of a binding.

access.default_rule: Deny read and write of a binding outside the steward, assigning agent, terminology operator and auditor roles; further restrict when sensitivity is set.
exceptions: Subject data owner may read bindings on their own subject.
Lawful statistical or clinical users may read specified facets under recorded purpose limitation.
Public catalog projections may publish non-sensitive dcat:theme IRIs without exposing provenance of automated classifiers.
audit_requirements: Log create, supersede, translate, validate and delete with agent, RFC 3339 event time and observation time.
Retain validation reports for the same period as the binding they attest.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md Name, Type and Specification URL to identify this Classification Binding package.
Read Storage type URL to learn the projection (for example document store, graph, or files) without treating that projection as semantics.
Read Interface URL for query and validation operations.
Read Processes URL for assign, validate, supersede and align workflows.
Then load authorised scheme lists and element-binding specifications before creating or inspecting bindings.

coverage.claim: This pattern covers the defensible union of instance classification assignment (ISO/IEC 11179 classifiable item to scheme item; FHIR Coding/CodeableConcept; DCAT theme; DCMI subject; ISO 19115 keywords) and element terminology binding (FHIR binding strength and value set), with lifecycle, version pinning, provenance, validation and access. It does not claim that any Dimension implementation conforms to FHIR, SKOS, ISO 11179, DCAT or GSIM.

checklist.notes: Binding master id, IRI and Dimension UUID are specified; scheme URI plus code or concept IRI identify the item; dates are excluded as identifiers.
Assignment status, supersession, dual-running during scheme revision, retired-code preservation and GSIM-aligned item change types are in scope.
Subject, scheme, item, value set, translations, mappings and facet relationships are modelled as references, not as owned scheme content.
Effective period versus observation/ingestion time, RFC 3339 with offset or Z, and scheme version as time-of-choice are specified.
Classifier agent, userSelected, method, evidence and review follow ISO/IEC 11179 registration goals and FHIR Coding.userSelected.
Binding owner is distinct from scheme custodian; steward and subject data owner roles are defined.
Code-in-system, value-set expansion membership, exclusivity, case rules and prohibition on display-as-key are specified.
Default deny, sensitivity, roles, scopes at bundle/layer/finding/artifact, and audit of sensitive reads are specified.
Superseded bindings are retained; hard delete is an exceptional, justified erasure with tombstone.
Alignments to SKOS, FHIR, ISO 11179, DCMI, DCAT, ISO 19115 and GSIM are recorded as alignments with documented conflicts.
FHIR required, extensible, preferred and example strengths are modelled as element-binding policy, not as instance codes.
Version pinning, versionNeeded and concept permanence versus GSIM version-as-object are covered, including virtual versus real change.
GSIM exclusivity, DCAT multi-theme and ISO 19115 overlapping topic categories are treated as slot policy, not a global axiom.
Scheme display, SKOS labels, user text and uncoded literals are distinguished; display is not a computable key.
Theme versus type/genre versus keyword type versus statistical variable coding are separate facets.
Jurisdiction of the scheme (NAICS/NACE/ISIC and similar) is recorded; place as an ISO 19115 keyword type is a facet, not a geometry model.
TLP, CUI and ISO/IEC 27001 information-security labels are a different sense of classification and are excluded; access control on subject-matter bindings remains in scope.

known_omissions: XKOS (DDI Alliance SKOS extension for statistical classifications) is widely cited for levels, correspondence and ruling notes, but the W3C TR URL returned 404 during this run; GSIM 2.0 is used as the statistical primary instead.

ISO/IEC 11179-3:2023 Classification package classes (Classification_Scheme, Classification_Scheme_Item, item_classification) are cited via Part 1 terms sourced from Part 3; the full Part 3 metamodel text was not retrieved.
ISO 25964 thesaurus model, UN/CEFACT CCTS classification, GS1 GPC and SNOMED CT compositional grammar are not developed as first-class findings.
No primary standard retrieved here defines calibrated confidence for machine-learned classification; confidence is marked locally defined.

Negative classification (explicit not-this-class), part-versus-whole classification, and legal determination artefacts (court or regulator classification orders) lack primary support in the retrieved sources.
OWL class assertion versus SKOS tagging is bounded but not fully mapped to description-logic instance checking.
conflicts: GSIM and UN statistical practice treat categories as mutually exclusive and exhaustive; DCAT allows multiple themes and SKOS allows polyhierarchy. Slot policy must choose; neither rule is universal.
FHIR concept identity is system URI plus code (version when needed); SKOS and DCMI prefer a concept URI; ISO/IEC 11179 uses registry identifiers. All three are aligned, not merged.
FHIR allows omitting code-system version when meaning is stable; GSIM treats each Statistical Classification version as a distinct object.
dcterms:type (nature/genre) versus dcterms:subject / dcat:theme (topic) are different facets; collapsing them loses DCAT and DCMI distinctions.
DCAT 3 dropped an explicit OWL range on dcat:theme; earlier DCAT text ranged theme to skos:Concept. Implementations must not claim a closed range.
ISO 19115 MD_TopicCategoryCode documents overlaps among high-level categories; that contradicts exclusivity assumptions from statistical classifications.
The English word binding in FHIR means an element constraint; classification in ISO 11179 means an assignment. This model unions both and keeps them as distinct layers so they are not collapsed.
regional_assumptions: HL7 Terminology Authority and terminology.hl7.org URI allocation apply to FHIR-centric health code systems and are not a global naming authority for ISIC, NACE, NAICS or ISO 19115 topic categories.
NACE is the usual activity classification in the EU; NAICS in the USMCA area; ISIC is the UN reference. Jurisdiction must be explicit on economic-activity bindings.
INSPIRE implementing rules in Europe constrain how ISO 19115 keywords and controlled vocabularies appear in spatial metadata; they are a regional profile, not the core pattern.
Lexical language tags follow BCP 47 as used by SKOS and FHIR; no single official language is assumed.
UNECE GSIM 2.0 (November 2024) is taken as the current statistical information-model authority; national adaptations of GSIM item-change types may differ.
adversarial_checks: Could this model be only FHIR Coding? No. Coding is the instance payload; the pattern also covers element binding strength, ISO 11179 classifiable-item association, DCAT themes, geospatial keywords and statistical variable coding.
Could this duplicate a Concept Scheme model? No. Schemes, hierarchies and editorial notes are referenced siblings; this pattern is the assignment and the slot constraint.
Could Identifier absorb this pattern because both use system plus a token? No. FHIR distinguishes Identifier.value from Coding.code; using dates or display as identifiers is forbidden.
Could security classification absorb this pattern? No. Sensitivity of a subject-matter code is an access concern; TLP/CUI labels are out of scope.
Does uncoded text break the model? No. DCMI and DCAT allow literals and keywords as degraded forms with recommended later URI alignment.

Does dual-running during ISIC or similar revisions contradict a single-class invariant? It contradicts GSIM exclusivity at a point in time unless policy allows a transition window; that window is an explicit lifecycle case, not an unstated default.
Is universal completeness claimed? No. XKOS, full ISO 11179-3, post-coordination grammars and ML confidence remain documented gaps.
